title: Spatially explicit feature importance for building height estimation using research-access high-resolution SAR and optical sensors
abstract: arXiv:2608.17822v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurate building height information at the individual footprint scale is essential for material stock accounting and post-disaster damage assessments yet remains difficult to obtain at city scale in the Global South where airborne LiDAR coverage is rare and commercial very high-resolution imagery is cost-prohibitive or unavailable. While recent works have demonstrated building height estimation using freely available Sentinel imagery, the resolution ceiling of resulting products is still coarse for material stock analysis. This study incorporates products derived from data freely accessible under scientific research licenses, TerraSAR-X StripMap and PlanetScope, alongside Sentinel-1 to predict building heights in a large city in Brazil. To account for the spatial autocorrelation in the training set, features from all sources are integrated in a geographically weighted random forest model, returning an RMSE of 5.34 m and R2 of 0.756 ag

translated_title: 基于研究级高分辨率SAR与光学传感器数据，空间显式特征重要性在建筑物高度估算中的应用
translated_abstract: 摘要：在个体足迹尺度上精确的建筑物高度信息对于材料存量核算和灾后损害评估至关重要，但在全球南方城市尺度上，由于机载LiDAR覆盖稀少且商业超高分辨率影像成本高昂或不可用，这一信息仍难以获取。尽管近期研究已利用免费获取的Sentinel影像实现了建筑物高度估算，但其产品分辨率上限对于材料存量分析而言仍显粗糙。本研究整合了在科研许可下免费获取的数据产品，包括TerraSAR-X StripMap和PlanetScope，以及Sentinel-1，用于预测巴西一个大城市的建筑物高度。为考虑训练集中的空间自相关性，所有来源的特征被整合进一个地理加权随机森林模型中，该模型返回的均方根误差（RMSE）为5.34米，决定系数（R²）为0.756。
tldr: 本研究首次将TerraSAR-X、PlanetScope与Sentinel-1数据整合进地理加权随机森林模型，在巴西大城市实现了高精度建筑物高度估算（RMSE 5.34米），并利用空间显式特征重要性方法揭示了各传感器在不同区域对估算贡献的差异。
en_tdlr: This study is the first to integrate TerraSAR-X, PlanetScope, and Sentinel-1 data into a geographically weighted random forest model, achieving high-accuracy building height estimation (RMSE 5.34 m) in a large Brazilian city, and utilizes spatially explicit feature importance to reveal the varying contributions of each sensor across different regions.
